title: Hány éjszakára? Booking for a Number of Nights

sections.title: Saying how long you're staying
sections.content: You already use -ra/-re for how long a ticket is valid. Booking a hotel room works the same way: put a number of nights in front of éjszaka and add -ra/-re to say how long you want the room for. egy éjszakára ("for one night"), két éjszakára ("for two nights"), egy hétre ("for a week"). The question is Hány éjszakára? — "For how many nights?"

items.spanish: Szeretnék foglalni egy szobát három éjszakára.
items.english: I'd like to book a room for three nights.

items.spanish: Hány éjszakára van szüksége a szobára?
items.english: For how many nights do you need the room?

sections.content: -ra/-re says how long something is booked or valid FOR, not until when — that's what -ig is for. Két éjszakára foglalok szobát ("I'm booking a room for two nights") tells you the length of the stay, not the date it ends.
